newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer after modest correction.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer after modest correction.

text.p: COMEX copper ended firmer, the market correcting modestly from the heavy, fund-led selloff in the previous session when prices fell too far, brokers said.
"There did not seem to be any fundamental reason for the market to drop so much, and was overextended on the downside," David Rinehimer of Smith Barney said.
"Who wants to be short down at these price levels when you have very tight inventory levels?" Rinehimer added.
LME stocks fell 2,775 tonnes Friday to 174,445 tonnes.
Although the dip was less than traders expected, the overall stock figure is still low, with several potential disruptions to production lurking in the background.
However, one analyst said he would be a seller at above 110.00 cents in the May contract.
May COMEX copper settled 1.50 cents firmer at 108.30 cents per pound, traded 109.10 to 107.75 cents.
Volume was estimated at 12,000 lots compared to Thursday's heavy 20,015 lots.
The International Copper Study Group said the market was in surplus by 33,000 tonnes of refined metal in January, compared to 96,000 tonnes in December.
